title: Strict henselization at a point with DVR local ring
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $y\in Y$, and suppose the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar x}$ be the strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with the canonical ring map $\iota:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar x}$ induced by the maps $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A_V$ of the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V,\bar v)$ factoring through an affine open of $y$. Then $\iota$ is a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] local homomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] (hence injective), and $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a discrete valuation ring if and only if $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar x}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr), first and third conditions, combined with etale-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring) identifying O^sh_{Y,xbar} with the strict henselization of O_{Y,y}, and the flatness of R -> R^sh (More on Algebra, Tag 07QM)

proof.text: Choose an affine open U=Spec A containing y, with corresponding prime p, so O_{Y,y}=A_p. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], the pointed affine etale-neighbourhood colimit defining O^sh_{Y,xbar} [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is the colimit over etale triples (B,q,phi). By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], this colimit is the ring strict henselization R^sh of R=A_p, with the same structural map iota and a local maximal ideal over the maximal ideal of R. This is the identification of Stacks 04HX; it respects the canonical maps from each neighbourhood ring.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), proof: affine chart and colimit of etale triples

proof.text: The triples of Step 1 form a filtered index category and every ring B in their diagram is etale over A (not over R=A_p) [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], applied to the ring A and its prime p. Each such B is a flat A-module by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. The underlying A-module of the ring colimit C=R^sh is the filtered colimit of these modules, so [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] makes R^sh a flat A-module. By the maximal-ideal assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], C is local with maximal ideal m_C whose preimage in A is p; hence every element of A outside p maps to a unit of C, A -> C factors uniquely through iota: A_p -> C, and iota is local (the preimage of m_C in A_p is pA_p). For an A_p-module M one has C (x)_{A_p} M = C (x)_A M, since A -> A_p is an epimorphism of rings; so tensoring with C over A_p is exact on A_p-modules and iota is flat. Thus iota is a flat local homomorphism of local rings, hence faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective], and the I=0 case of [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] makes it injective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QM (lemma-henselization-properties), proof of (1); Algebra Tags 00U2, 05UT and 05CK

proof.text: Assume R is a DVR. It has dimension one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one]. Since R is Noetherian, [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] makes R^sh Noetherian. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], dim R^sh=1. Since a DVR has a principal maximal ideal, it is regular local of dimension one by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and [def-weil-regular-scheme]; [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] makes R^sh regular local. Apply [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] to conclude that R^sh is a DVR.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr), proof via Tags 06LJ, 06LK, 06LN and Algebra Tag 00PD

proof.text: Conversely assume R^sh is a DVR. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], it has dimension one. [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] gives dim R=1; [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] reflects regularity from R^sh to R. Here R^sh is regular local because its maximal ideal is principal [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and its dimension is one [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since R is Noetherian by hypothesis, [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] now makes R a DVR. The identification in Step 1 converts these two implications into the asserted equivalence for the scheme local rings.
